clue.text: Contemporary dependent on those of little stature

parts.note: a decision that is up to someone depends on them
the minute, as a noun phrase, means tiny people, those of small size

explanation.surface: A modern person who relies on the patronage of titled grandees.
explanation.walkthrough: The minute (pronounced my-NEWT) are read as a group of people, as in 'the rich'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bang up to date is current, so it is contemporary.

clue.text: Where the rudder is, not out in the open

definitions.meaning: the counter is the overhanging stern of a ship, and the rudder sits beneath it
goods sold furtively are kept out of sight below the shop's counter

explanation.definitionFit: Illicit trade is done secretly, hidden from view rather than openly displayed; nautically the rudder hangs beneath the stern overhang.

clue.text: Greek character joining the volunteers

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: A Greek man signs up with the reserve soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' means a letter of the alphabet, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is the eighth letter of the Greek alphabet, and a letter is a character.

clue.text: The drains must be fixed, being befouled

indicators.note: fixing something puts it back in order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Blocked drains need repair because they have become filthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must be fixed' rearranges the letters of THE DRAINS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tainted or sullied has been dirtied, just as befouled things have.

clue.text: He turns out as, ultimately, the winner

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word the

parts.note: a victor is the one who wins

explanation.surface: A man evicts someone, coming out on top in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' takes only the final letter of 'the'; 'as' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who expels a tenant from a property is one who turns them out.

clue.text: Out of place in record time

parts.note: taken as written
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: Something unsuitable crops up in a record-breaking time.
explanation.definitionFit: A clumsy, inappropriate remark is unsuitable, so it is out of place.

clue.text: Releases two articles in French about successful action

indicators.note: about says the two French words go round the other piece

parts.note: UN and LES are French articles, 'a' and 'the'
a coup is a successful stroke or move

explanation.surface: A French sentence uses two articles about a triumph to free something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Successful action' is the French loan word for a sudden triumphant stroke, fitting the French theme of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Detaching railway carriages or a trailer frees them, so it releases them.

clue.text: This account is what shocks the beak

parts.note: an electric current is what gives a person a shock
a bird's beak is its bill

explanation.surface: A household invoice is so steep it gives a magistrate a jolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beak' is also British slang for a magistrate, which the surface plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: A power invoice from the utility company is an account to be paid.

clue.text: One gets benefit, though not old or unemployed

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: not says the letter for old is dropped from the benefit word

parts.note: the dole is British state benefit for the jobless

explanation.surface: Someone collects welfare payments despite being young and out of work.
explanation.definitionFit: A person without work is inactive, out of a job, as the jobless are.

clue.text: Erect? Just the opposite, by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the word is heard, not seen, giving a spelling that sounds alike

parts.note: to raze a building is to flatten it, the reverse of putting it up

explanation.surface: A one-word question about building, with a quibbling reply.
explanation.walkthrough: RAZE, the opposite of erect, is said aloud and gives a word meaning erect itself.
explanation.definitionFit: To build or put up a structure is to elevate it.

clue.text: Team expressed unrestrained glee

definitions.meaning: a group working together, as on a ship
a past tense of crow, to boast or exult loudly

explanation.definitionFit: A ship's company is a working group; and the old past tense of crow means exulted loudly.

clue.text: Player given terrible roasting

indicators.note: a terrible version is a mangled one, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A performer gets a scathing critical review.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' rearranges the letters of ROASTING.
explanation.definitionFit: A church musician at the keyboard is a performer who plays an instrument.

clue.text: Reliable, though at first impaired by neglect

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of though

parts.note: skills left unused become rusty

explanation.surface: Something dependable, although it was spoilt early on by lack of care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' takes the opening letter of 'though'.
explanation.definitionFit: A faithful, dependable servant or tool can be trusted.

clue.text: Grey place in the Yukon

definitions.meaning: a grey horse is often called a ...
the capital of Canada's Yukon territory

explanation.definitionFit: Horse people call a pale grey animal a white horse; and that name is also the Yukon's capital city.

clue.text: Four-letter word from Peggy, upset about temperature

indicators.note: about says the name goes round the other piece
in a down clue upset turns the name upside down, so it reads backwards

parts.note: Peggy is a pet form of the name Margaret

explanation.surface: Peggy, cross about the heat, utters a swear word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns MARGARET into TERAGRAM, which goes round T.
explanation.definitionFit: A tetragram is any word made of four letters; 'four-letter word' usually suggests swearing, which the surface plays on.

clue.text: There's always a place for putting a box, for example

parts.note: ever means always
the green is where golfers putt

explanation.surface: A golf course always has room for a container.
explanation.walkthrough: Box is a shrub, not a container; 'putting' is golf, not placing.
explanation.definitionFit: The box shrub keeps its leaves all year, so it is an example of an evergreen plant.

clue.text: Ignoring the odds. Olga and Linda bet

indicators.note: ignoring the odds means skipping the odd-numbered letters and keeping the even ones

explanation.surface: Two women wager without caring about the odds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ignoring the odds' keeps the second and fourth letters of OLGA and LINDA; 'and' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A wager was placed, as in 'laid a fiver on the horse'.

clue.text: Labour organisation's turned tail

indicators.note: turned says the letters are read backwards

parts.note: the TUC is the Trades Union Congress, Britain's union federation; the 's adds S

explanation.surface: A union body has done an about-turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses TUCS.
explanation.definitionFit: The short upright tail of a rabbit or deer is called a scut.

clue.text: Has replied in order to get post as a salesman

indicators.note: put in order means the letters are rearranged into a proper arrangement

explanation.surface: An applicant answers a job ad for a sales role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in order' rearranges the letters of HAS REPLIED.
explanation.definitionFit: A dealer is a salesman, and his position or business is the dealership.

clue.text: Pastiche not hard to rewrite as suitable for theatre

indicators.note: rewriting the remaining letters reorders them
not says the letter for hard is taken out of pastiche

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: An imitative work needs reworking before it can be staged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not hard' removes H from PASTICHE, and 'to rewrite' rearranges PASTICE. Theatre is the operating theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Sterile, germ-free conditions are what an operating theatre needs.

clue.text: Shrub of specified sort mother put in

indicators.note: put in says mother goes inside the other word

parts.note: such means of the kind already mentioned
MA is mother

explanation.surface: Mother plants a particular kind of bush.
explanation.walkthrough: Sumach is the British spelling; Americans usually write sumac.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumach is a shrub or small tree grown for its red autumn leaves and spice.

clue.text: Jack wearing belt as customary attire

indicators.note: wearing says one piece is inside the other, which wraps it like clothing

parts.note: to belt someone is to hit them
a jack tar is a sailor, as is an AB, able seaman

explanation.surface: A sailor in a belt as his usual dress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack' is a sailor, as in jack tar, not a playing card or a name.
explanation.definitionFit: A monk's or nun's robe, the usual dress of an order, is a habit.

clue.text: Insertion of a word like this by no means straightforward?

definitions.text: Insertion of a word like this by no means straightforward?

parts.words: Insertion of a word like this by no means straightforward?
parts.note: squeezing a remark into a non-stop talker's flow is hard, and the word also means sideways, not straight on

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is getting a word in sideways, with difficulty; the word also means side first.

clue.text: Composer using computer link with hesitation

parts.note: the web links computers across the world
er is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: A composer works on a computer network, haltingly.
explanation.definitionFit: Carl Maria von Weber was a German Romantic composer.

clue.text: The way I run a prison

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way
taken as written
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A governor explains his method of managing a jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Stir is slang for prison, as in 'doing time in stir'.

clue.text: Flatter, truncated type of hill in America

indicators.note: truncated means cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: to butter someone up is to flatter them

explanation.surface: A flatter, flat-topped kind of American hill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flatter' looks like a comparative adjective, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A butte is an isolated flat-topped hill in the western USA.

clue.text: Some superb rigging in this vessel

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Admiring the fine ropes and sails on this ship.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sits inside the clue's own framing: the vessel is the one with the fine rigging.
explanation.definitionFit: A brig is a two-masted square-rigged sailing ship.

clue.text: Electromotor' 'worked without new zapper

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the jumbled letters go round the other piece
worked means manipulated, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: An electric motor running without a fresh device for switching channels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worked' rearranges ELECTROMOTOR and 'without' puts those letters around N.
explanation.definitionFit: A zapper is slang for the handset used to change TV channels.
